clue.text: Fiddle, causing embarrassment

definitions.meaning: to play a fiddle badly is to saw or scratch at the strings
an awkward predicament one has got into

explanation.surface: Someone cheats and is caught, to their shame.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle roughly is to scratch a bow across strings, and a tight spot of trouble is also this word.

clue.text: The monk's transport alternative

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old UK national railway
an alternative is another or other choice

explanation.surface: A friar chooses some other way of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: BR stands for British Rail, the former national railway of Britain; the 's after 'monk' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a religious order address one another by this family title.

clue.text: A right not exercised in a boy's support

indicators.note: the first group of letters is set in the middle of the boy's word

parts.note: a page is a boy attendant

indicators.note: exercised suggests the letters are worked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone holds back from using a privilege while backing a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' is the definition; 'exercised' rearranges the right letter with 'not', and a page boy's attendant word goes around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronage is backing or sponsorship given by a benefactor.

clue.text: Many little streams make furrows

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, so a large number
rills are small brooks

explanation.surface: Numerous small brooks cut channels in the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving D relies on the Roman numeral 500; 'make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a shallow furrow in which seeds are sown.

clue.text: A cry to join King Charles's entourage

indicators.note: an entourage surrounds its royal, so the join word wraps the king's letters

parts.note: a seam is where two pieces are joined
CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles in Latin

explanation.surface: Someone shouts to be allowed into the royal retinue.
explanation.walkthrough: King Charles's cipher comes from Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles; 'entourage' makes the join word surround it, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shriek is a loud piercing cry.

clue.text: A man of rank getting wrong gear sent

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in the incorrect order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer is annoyed that the wrong kit has been delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' signals rearranging GEAR SENT; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer holds a rank above corporal.

clue.text: Quickly took steps against the opposition

definitions.text: Quickly took steps against the opposition

parts.words: Quickly took steps against the opposition
parts.note: reads as taking prompt action against rivals, but describes running fast in a contest with opponents

explanation.surface: Someone acted fast to counter their rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Competing in a running contest means running at speed against opponents.

clue.text: A summary might well be appropriate

definitions.meaning: a short précis of a paper
verb: to take for oneself, steal

explanation.surface: A précis seems a suitable thing to write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning to take away or steal; 'might well be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis of an article is its abstract, and to remove or purloin something is to abstract it.

clue.text: Sea-rovers' coarse-sounding arrogance

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word before is taken by how it is said

parts.note: coarse is pronounced like the first part of the answer
airs are a show of superiority

explanation.surface: Pirates are rough and haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbary pirates were privateers who roamed the seas.

clue.text: Before one's placed in the church it should be correct

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before

indicators.note: placed in says one piece is set inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
one is I, and one's means I is

explanation.surface: Something must be right before it is installed in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is I + S (I is); 'placed in' puts it inside CE, the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and accurate both describe something without error.

clue.text: The sailor's after a number as being a focus of devotion

indicators.note: after puts the sailor at the end, following the other letters

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty
tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman follows a figure who is the object of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' gives L, the Roman numeral 50; 'The' and 's are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The communion table in a church is where worship is directed.

clue.text: Money expended on green day make-up which is truly fantastic

indicators.note: the money is spent on what follows, so it is placed in front

parts.note: L is the symbol for a pound, from Latin libra

indicators.note: make-up suggests the letters are composed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Cash is spent on cosmetics for a festive day, which is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: L for pound sterling comes from libra; 'make-up' rearranges GREEN DAY into EGENDARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something storied enough to be the stuff of myth is fabulous.

clue.text: A letter written in most expressive language

indicators.note: written in says the letters are inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A letter is composed in highly emotive words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' is a link; the letters sit in the middle of 'expressive'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the nineteenth letter of the alphabet is spelt out like this.

clue.text: At the end of the day the head makes a regular appearance

parts.words: At the end of the day
parts.note: even is an old word for evening, the end of the day
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Every evening the headmaster shows up as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: EVEN is poetic for evening; NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniformity is a smooth, level, regular look.

clue.text: Warning given to nice eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: An odd person is given a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges TO NICE; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Advance notification of something is a warning.

clue.text: Ladies who really enjoy a good row!

definitions.text: Ladies who really enjoy a good row!

parts.words: Ladies who really enjoy a good row!
parts.note: row looks like a quarrel but is the rowing of a boat

explanation.surface: Some women love a good argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Female rowers pull oars in a boat.

clue.text: Such dogs can be frisky some days

indicators.note: frisky means lively, so the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: Pet dogs are lively on certain days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be frisky' rearranges SOME DAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siberian breed of white sled dog.

clue.text: Acquire some luggage that's lightweight

indicators.note: some means a part of the words that follow, which contain the letters

explanation.surface: Buy some baggage that's light to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the end of 'luggage' and the start of 'that's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain or come by something.

clue.text: Taking look after look shows sense

indicators.note: after places the first look-word behind the second

parts.note: to eye is to look at
a sight is a look, as in catch sight of

explanation.surface: Glancing again and again shows good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look after look' puts the first look's synonym after the second's; 'Taking' and 'shows' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses.

clue.text: A Greek character fed the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the word for fed is read backwards

parts.note: fed means ate a meal

explanation.surface: A Greek person was given food in the wrong manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' reverses ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Exclude the field of corn

parts.note: to bar is to keep out
a ley is a meadow or grassland field

explanation.surface: Keep someone out of the cornfield.
explanation.walkthrough: LEY (or lea) is grassland; 'corn' in British usage covers any cereal crop.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain any cereal grain is called corn, and this one is used for malting.

clue.text: Try to be like a quiet egghead

parts.note: p is piano, quiet in music
the head of the word egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: Try to imitate a reserved intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' is read as the head of 'egg', its first letter, not as an intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate or mimic someone.

clue.text: A note added willingly

parts.note: willingly looks like gladly but means to a will, a testament

explanation.surface: A message is attached gladly.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement to a testament amending it.

clue.text: The utterance of a friend

parts.note: a sentry asks friend or foe, and a friend proves it by speaking a secret word

explanation.surface: Something said by a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word spoken to a sentry to be let through as an ally.

clue.text: It may appear a hero's landed!

indicators.note: the letters may show up in another form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of a hero's, including the s

explanation.surface: Apparently a hero has come down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is taken as a letter here and rearranged with A HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Come on to land from the sea.

clue.text: Sprinkle sugar on the doctor giving a certain advantage

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
an edge is an advantage over someone

explanation.surface: The physician adds sweetener for a competitive boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving a certain' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dust food with powder such as flour or sugar.

clue.text: Limits MP surrounded by business fools

indicators.note: surrounded by says the MP is enclosed by the other letters

parts.note: Co. is company, a business
asses are idiots

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament is hemmed in by idiots in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' makes the company and fools pieces close round the Member of Parliament; 'Limits' means scope or range.
explanation.definitionFit: Range or scope, the bounds within which something lies.

clue.text: Set speed the inexperienced driver must stay within

indicators.note: stay within means the learner letter sits inside the speed word

parts.note: pace is rate of movement
L is the learner plate on a UK car

explanation.surface: A learner must keep within a fixed speed.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: To put or lay something down.

clue.text: She's round and full of energy

parts.note: O is round in shape
live means charged, lively

explanation.surface: A woman is plump and lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' defines a woman's first name; 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as in Olive Oyl.

clue.text: Upset when grenade exploded

indicators.note: exploded blows the letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Distress when a bomb went off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' rearranges GRENADE; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or throw into disorder.

clue.text: Scots crying for some form of recognition

definitions.meaning: in Scots to greet is to weep

explanation.surface: Scottish weeping as a way of saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scottish dialect 'greet' means to weep, so greeting is crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping in Scottish dialect, and a salutation acknowledging someone's arrival.

clue.text: Rise, of a quarter cent

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An increase of twenty-five per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarter is a compass point here, giving S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb or upward movement.
